thesis: This episode argues that General Motors (GM) represents a compelling investment opportunity based on a deep research process that identified the stock as significantly undervalued compared to its original acquisition cost. The speaker maintains a bullish stance on GM, noting that he still holds the position with gains exceeding 120% and that the company became cheaper than the price the original debtor paid.

claims.claim: The speaker decided to take a position in General Motors after realizing there were reasons why an investment in GM made sense, noting they still own the position and are up more than 120%.
claims.quote: And it dawned on me that there were a number of reasons why an investment in GM made all the sense in the world. And that led me to actually take a position in GM. And we still own that position. I don't have much to say about it, except that we're up, I don't know, more than 120% so far on that position.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Warren Buffett turned him down for a position in Exxon, noting that Buffett is his analyst at zero pay.
